items.title: Write player class characters concept prompts (4 images)
items.description:
## Why
The four class fantasies (constitution pillar: every class is a different way to play) must read by silhouette alone in the class lineup and at 30 m; these are the most-seen models in the game and the first style anchor.

## What
Write one prompt file per concept image in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: character) from `character-reference-sheet.md`, flat front-facing on plain parchment so the image-to-3D API gets clean input, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) verbatim, output spec and consistency checklist.

Turnaround reference sheets for knight, archer, sorcerer and thief per style bible §5.1 (primary shape, signature prop, palette accent), then Claude-run image-to-3D, retopo to 8–12 k tris, one 1024² atlas, rig on the canonical humanoid skeleton.

Concept image ids (4):
- `char-knight-base-01`
- `char-archer-base-01`
- `char-sorcerer-base-01`
- `char-thief-base-01`

Target model ids (4):
- `model-char-knight-01`
- `model-char-archer-01`
- `model-char-sorcerer-01`
- `model-char-thief-01`

## Scope
- In: Concept/reference prompt per id above
- In: Model output spec (tri budget, texture, bones) recorded in each prompt
- Out: 3D generation (`e37-asset-player-classes-3d-generate`)

## Notes
Milestone m2 (earlier than most assets) because the class-fantasy playtests (`e35-class-fantasy-tests`) read much better with real silhouettes, and these sheets are style anchors for `e37-asset-style-lock`. Gameplay still runs on `e37-greybox-asset-kit` placeholders until integration. Held weapons are a separate set (`e37-asset-weapons-*`). Thief disguise recolour lives in `e37-asset-thief-props-*`.

Budget: 8–12 k tris LOD0 + LOD1 50 %, one 1024² atlas, 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 4 concept ids, when the asset validator runs, then each has exactly one prompt file whose id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks.
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when compared with docs/art/style-bible.md §14 and §14.1, then the preamble and category add-on match byte-for-byte.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it records the §13.2 model budget (8–12 k tris LOD0 + LOD1 50 %, one 1024² atlas, 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2)) and the silhouette/palette rules from §5 relevant to the asset.
- AC-4 [content] Edge: given a prompt asking for perspective views, cast shadows or busy backgrounds that break image-to-3D, or containing text requests or an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails naming the file.

items.title: Generate player class characters concepts via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Image-to-3D quality depends on a clean, approved flat concept (style bible §17.2).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` for all 4 concept prompts into `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` + sidecar; self-check against the checklist (silhouette at 64 px, palette, flat lighting) and iterate; build the review page.

## Scope
- In: Concept generation and iteration log
- In: Silhouette test renders (solid ink at 64 px) on the review page
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-player-classes-concept-approve`)

## Notes
Record account tier in every sidecar.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 4 prompts, when the batch completes, then every id has `vN.png` + `vN.json` (prompt path, tool, model, tier, date) in `assets/_incoming/`.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when auto-checked, then it is front-facing on a plain parchment background with no cast shadows, or the iteration log records a regeneration.
- AC-3 [content] Given the review page, when opened, then each candidate shows alongside its solid-ink 64 px silhouette.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.

items.title: Owner approval: player class characters flat concepts
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the flat concept gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the 4 flat concept images and their silhouette tests and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: flat concept, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-player-classes-concept-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: each class is identifiable by silhouette alone when filled solid ink at 64 px tall, and the four read as one family in a side-by-side lineup. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 4 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "flat concept".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then each class is identifiable by silhouette alone when filled solid ink at 64 px tall, and the four read as one family in a side-by-side lineup.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-player-classes-concept-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

items.title: Generate player class characters 3D models via image-to-3D API
items.description:
## Why
The owner never does 3D work; Claude turns approved flats into game-ready models (contract §1).

## What
For each of the 4 target models: call `e37-3d-gen-api-client` (Meshy or Tripo per `e37-3d-pipeline-decision`) with the approved flat, remesh/retopo to budget, rig/animate via API where applicable, download to `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.glb`, run automated validation, and render turntables with `e37-turntable-preview`.

## Scope
- In: API jobs, retopo, rig
- In: Automated budget/naming/licence validation
- In: Turntable PNG strip + GIF per model
- Out: Turntable approval (`e37-asset-player-classes-turntable-approve`)

## Notes
Budget: 8–12 k tris LOD0 + LOD1 50 %, one 1024² atlas, 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2). API keys only from `MESHY_API_KEY` / `TRIPO_API_KEY` env vars.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the approved flats, when the API client runs, then each of the 4 model ids has a `vN.glb` + sidecar (provider, model version, tier, job id, date, source image hash) in `assets/_incoming/`.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each glb, when validated, then it meets 8–12 k tris LOD0 + LOD1 50 %, one 1024² atlas, 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2), or the job is re-run with adjusted retopo settings and the iteration log says why.
- AC-3 [integration] Given each glb, when `e37-turntable-preview` runs, then a PNG strip (8 angles) and a GIF exist for the review page.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given an API job that fails or times out, when the client retries with back-off, then at most 3 attempts are made, no duplicate paid job is started for an id with a completed job, and the failure is reported per id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given sidecars and logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key appears.

items.title: Integrate approved player class characters
items.description:
## Why
Final models replace greybox stand-ins without touching gameplay code (contract §5).

## What
Promote approved glbs through `e37-model-import-pipeline` (meshopt + KTX2, LODs), bind to the stylized material, wire into content data, add CREDITS rows and approval records for both gates, and swap out the placeholder models.

## Scope
- In: Import pipeline, LODs, material binding
- In: CREDITS + approval records (flat concept + turntable)
- In: Placeholder swap
- Out: Gameplay logic (consuming beads)

## Notes
Consumers: `e19-class-definitions`, `e02-animation-hooks`, `e37-animation-pipeline`, `e37-stylized-material`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the approved glbs, when the import pipeline and `e37-asset-validator` run, then all 4 models are under `public/assets/model/` within 8–12 k tris LOD0 + LOD1 50 %, one 1024² atlas, 1 material, ≤ 65 bones (style bible §13.2) and the validator is green.
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/CREDITS.md` and `assets/approvals.json`, when audited, then every model has a CREDITS row (provider, tier, date, prompt path, terms URL) and approval records for both the flat-concept and turntable gates.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the class-select scene, when each class is chosen, then its final model loads, plays idle/walk/run/attack from the retargeted clip set with no console errors, and a Playwright screenshot shows all four in the lineup.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the combat stress scene with these models, when `e32-perf-budgets` runs, then draw calls stay ≤ 150 and visible triangles ≤ 500 k on Low.
- AC-5 [integration] Edge: given a model with a turntable approval but a changed file hash, when CI runs, then integration is refused and the placeholder remains.

items.title: Write school frames and glyphs prompts (26 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Thirteen schools cannot be told apart by hue alone; the shared rim frame and glyph per school carry identity for colour-blind players (style bible §2.3, §9.2) and anchor every spell icon.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: icon-spell / ui) from template `spell-icon.md (frames) + ui-element.md (glyphs)`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

One painted medallion rim frame per school (school core/highlight/shadow colours, shape language from §2.3) and one flat ink-brush school glyph per school for grimoire ribbons, hotbar and book spines.

Asset ids (26):
- `ui-spell-frame-fire-01`

## Scope

items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 26 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.

## Why
Final art replaces placeholders without touching gameplay code (contract §5: integration is a file swap).

## What
Promote approved versions to `assets/source/<category>/<asset-id>/`, run the pipeline (atlas/KTX2 build as applicable), add `assets/CREDITS.md` rows and approval records, replace placeholder entries, and verify in-game.

## Scope
- In: Source promotion, pipeline run, atlas rebuild
- In: CREDITS rows + approval records in the same commit
- In: Clearing placeholder flags for this set
- Out: Gameplay/UI logic (owned by the consuming beads)

## Notes
Consumers: `e06-spell-hotbar-ui`, `e07-grimoire-ui`, `e06-spell-schema`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the approved sources, when the import pipeline and `e37-asset-validator` run, then runtime files exist under `public/assets/` for all 23 ids and the validator (naming, budgets, licence, approval hash) is green.
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/CREDITS.md`, when audited, then each id has a row with tool, model, account tier, date, prompt path and terms URL.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the placeholder manifest, when integration completes, then no id in this set is flagged `placeholder: true`.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the spell hotbar with all 23 spells assigned via debug console, when rendered at 1920×1080, then every slot shows its final icon (no placeholder flag) and no console errors occur.
- AC-5 [perf] Given the rebuilt atlases/textures, when `e32-perf-budgets` runs, then resident texture memory stays ≤ 256 MB on Low and the UI/fonts download share stays ≤ 4 MB where applicable.
- AC-6 [integration] Edge: given an id in this set without an approval record, when the pipeline runs, then it refuses to promote that id, the placeholder stays in place, and the remaining-placeholder report lists it.

items.title: Write menu kit and journal UI prompts (21 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Every menu (options, save/load, journal) shares the "illuminated field journal" look (style bible §9); one kit keeps them coherent and is the UI style anchor.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: ui) from template `ui-element.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Generic parchment 9-slice panel, button states, focus ring, slider, checkbox, scrollbar, tooltip and divider, plus the journal parchment frame, tab icons (quest, rumour, note), quest state icons (active, resolved, failed), new-entry toast, compass nudge glyph and objective marker.

Asset ids (21):
- `ui-panel-parchment-9slice-01`
- `ui-button-normal-01`
- `ui-button-hover-01`
- `ui-button-pressed-01`
- `ui-button-disabled-01`
- `ui-focus-ring-01`
- `ui-slider-01`
- `ui-checkbox-01`
- `ui-scrollbar-01`
- `ui-tooltip-9slice-01`
- `ui-divider-flourish-01`
- `ui-panel-journal-9slice-01`
- `ui-glyph-tab-quest-01`
- `ui-glyph-tab-rumour-01`
- `ui-glyph-tab-note-01`
- `ui-glyph-quest-active-01`
- `ui-glyph-quest-resolved-01`
- `ui-glyph-quest-failed-01`
- `ui-toast-journal-01`
- `ui-glyph-compass-nudge-01`
- `ui-marker-objective-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
The generic menu kit (panel/button/focus/slider/checkbox/scrollbar/tooltip/divider) is not in `plan/gameplay-asset-needs.md` but every menu bead needs it; added here. Wayfinding glyphs also serve `e23-wayfinding-hints` (P2). m2 because it is one of the three style-anchor sets. Focus ring must satisfy `e31-menu-navigation` visible-focus contrast.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 21 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (1024² generate, transparent, 9-slice insets recorded per frame, glyphs flat single-colour 64²) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: panels tile cleanly under 9-slice stretch from 200 px to 1600 px wide and body text on panels meets ≥ 7:1 contrast (§9).
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate menu kit and journal UI via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 21 prompt files of `e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 1024² generate, transparent, 9-slice insets recorded per frame, glyphs flat single-colour 64². Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 21 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (1024² generate, transparent, 9-slice insets recorded per frame, glyphs flat single-colour 64²), then dimensions, transparency/background and grid layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Owner approval: menu kit and journal UI
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 21 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: image, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: panels tile cleanly under 9-slice stretch from 200 px to 1600 px wide and body text on panels meets ≥ 7:1 contrast (§9). Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 21 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "image".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then panels tile cleanly under 9-slice stretch from 200 px to 1600 px wide and body text on panels meets ≥ 7:1 contrast (§9).
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

items.title: Write player weapons concept prompts (12 images)
items.description:
## Why
Each class has one signature prop always visible in silhouette (shield, bow, staff, hood) — the weapons carry the class fantasy and must match the approved character sheets.

## What
Write one prompt file per concept image in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: prop) from `prop-sheet.md`, flat front-facing on plain parchment so the image-to-3D API gets clean input, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) verbatim, output spec and consistency checklist.

One flat front-facing concept image per held weapon or arrow variant (sword, wood and metal shields, bow, daggers, staff/focus, standard + fire/water/rope/noise/blunt arrows), then Claude-run image-to-3D (or CC0 kit match), retopo to 300–1.5 k tris, sharing the character or prop atlas.

Concept image ids (12):
- `prop-weapon-sword-01`
- `prop-weapon-shield-wood-01`
- `prop-weapon-shield-metal-01`
- `prop-weapon-bow-01`
- `prop-weapon-dagger-01`
- `prop-weapon-staff-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-standard-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-fire-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-water-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-rope-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-noise-01`
- `prop-weapon-arrow-blunt-01`

Target model ids (12):
- `model-weapon-sword-01`
- `model-weapon-shield-wood-01`
- `model-weapon-shield-metal-01`
- `model-weapon-bow-01`
- `model-weapon-dagger-01`
- `model-weapon-staff-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-standard-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-fire-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-water-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-rope-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-noise-01`
- `model-weapon-arrow-blunt-01`

## Scope
- In: Concept/reference prompt per id above
- In: Model output spec (tri budget, texture, bones) recorded in each prompt
- Out: 3D generation (`e37-asset-weapons-3d-generate`)

## Notes
m2 alongside the class models (a knight without a sword breaks the class playtests). Arrow variants are one shaft with swappable heads/payloads where possible. Concept images are one object per image (image-to-3D friendly), not a multi-object sheet. Post-MVP trick arrows (`e05-trick-arrows-extended`) are out.

Budget: 300–1.5 k tris per held weapon, arrows ≤ 300, no LODs, character or prop atlas, shared material (style bible §13.2).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 12 concept ids, when the asset validator runs, then each has exactly one prompt file whose id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks.
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when compared with docs/art/style-bible.md §14 and §14.1, then the preamble and category add-on match byte-for-byte.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it records the §13.2 model budget (300–1.5 k tris per held weapon, arrows ≤ 300, no LODs, character or prop atlas, shared material (style bible §13.2)) and the silhouette/palette rules from §5 relevant to the asset.
- AC-4 [content] Edge: given a prompt asking for perspective views, cast shadows or busy backgrounds that break image-to-3D, or containing text requests or an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails naming the file.

items.title: Generate player weapons 3D models via image-to-3D API
items.description:
## Why
The owner never does 3D work; Claude turns approved flats into game-ready models (contract §1).

## What
For each of the 12 target models: call `e37-3d-gen-api-client` (Meshy or Tripo per `e37-3d-pipeline-decision`) with the approved flat, remesh/retopo to budget, rig/animate via API where applicable, download to `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.glb`, run automated validation, and render turntables with `e37-turntable-preview`.

## Scope
- In: API jobs, retopo, rig
- In: Automated budget/naming/licence validation
- In: Turntable PNG strip + GIF per model
- Out: Turntable approval (`e37-asset-weapons-turntable-approve`)

## Notes
Budget: 300–1.5 k tris per held weapon, arrows ≤ 300, no LODs, character or prop atlas, shared material (style bible §13.2). API keys only from `MESHY_API_KEY` / `TRIPO_API_KEY` env vars.
items.acceptance:

- AC-3 [integration] Given each glb, when `e37-turntable-preview` runs, then a PNG strip (8 angles) and a GIF exist for the review page.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given an API job that fails or times out, when the client retries with back-off, then at most 3 attempts are made, no duplicate paid job is started for an id with a completed job, and the failure is reported per id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given sidecars and logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key appears.

items.title: Generate spellbook covers via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 24 prompt files of `e37-asset-book-covers-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-book-covers-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: cover 2:3 1024×1536, transparent around the book object, blank title plate, text-safe rectangle recorded. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 24 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (cover 2:3 1024×1536, transparent around the book object, blank title plate, text-safe rectangle recorded), then dimensions, transparency/background and grid layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Generate elemental spell VFX via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 18 prompt files of `e37-asset-vfx-spells-elemental-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-vfx-spells-elemental-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 1024² sheet, 4×4 or 8×8 exact grid, black background for additive cores (alpha for smoke/steam), 12–24 fps. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 18 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (1024² sheet, 4×4 or 8×8 exact grid, black background for additive cores (alpha for smoke/steam), 12–24 fps), then dimensions, transparency/background and grid layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

items.title: Write combat impact VFX prompts (10 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Souls-like weight lives in the moment of impact; material-specific hits tell the player what they struck and whether the parry landed.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: vfx) from template `vfx-flipbook-texture.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Impact flipbooks by material (metal sparks, wood splinters, bone dust, ichor puff, stone chips), block spark, parry flash, guard-break shatter, critical burst and arrow deflect sparks.

Asset ids (10):
- `vfx-hit-spark-metal-01`
- `vfx-hit-splinter-wood-01`
- `vfx-hit-bone-dust-01`
- `vfx-hit-ichor-puff-01`
- `vfx-hit-stone-chips-01`
- `vfx-block-spark-01`
- `vfx-parry-flash-01`
- `vfx-guard-break-shatter-01`
- `vfx-critical-burst-01`
- `vfx-deflect-sparks-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-vfx-combat-impacts-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
m2 because combat feel is validated in `e04-skeleton-fun-validation` / `e35-class-fantasy-tests`; the procedural placeholders still keep gameplay unblocked. No gore: ichor is a stylised puff. Parry flash obeys the ≤ 25 % screen-area flash rule.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 10 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).

- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (1024² sheet, 4×4 exact grid, black background for additive sparks/flashes, alpha for dust/chips, 18–24 fps, non-looping) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: each material hit is distinguishable without sound and parry flash is clearly different from a normal block.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 13 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: image, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-vfx-elemental-destruction-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: each element state is identifiable in greyscale by shape and motion, and crack stages read as progressively weaker. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 13 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "image".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then each element state is identifiable in greyscale by shape and motion, and crack stages read as progressively weaker.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-vfx-elemental-destruction-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/CREDITS.md`, when audited, then each id has a row with tool, model, account tier, date, prompt path and terms URL.

items.title: Write ambient environment VFX prompts (5 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Ambient motion makes the hand-painted world feel alive and warm without costing gameplay budget.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: vfx) from template `vfx-flipbook-texture.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Dust motes in light shafts, torch embers, fireflies, falling leaves and a painted fog-volume noise texture.

Asset ids (5):
- `vfx-env-dust-motes-01`
- `vfx-env-torch-embers-01`
- `vfx-env-fireflies-01`
- `vfx-env-falling-leaves-01`
- `vfx-env-fog-volume-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-vfx-environment-ambient-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

## Notes
P2 to match `e29-environment-fx`. Location-specific ambient VFX from the world list are out of scope here.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 5 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (512² sheets or single sprites, alpha background, loopable) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: ambient effects stay subtle (never mistaken for gameplay cues).
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate ambient environment VFX via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 5 prompt files of `e37-asset-vfx-environment-ambient-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-vfx-environment-ambient-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 512² sheets or single sprites, alpha background, loopable. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 5 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (512² sheets or single sprites, alpha background, loopable), then dimensions, transparency/background and grid layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

Players manage their kit in the inventory and quick slots; every starting weapon, arrow type and thief tool needs a readable icon that matches its world model.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset in `assets/prompts/<category>/<asset-id>.md` (category: icon-item) from template `item-icon.md`, with the GPT STYLE PREAMBLE (style bible §14) plus its §14.1 category add-on pasted verbatim, the output spec, the bible consistency checklist, consuming bead(s) and an empty iteration log.

Painted ¾ top-down item icons for the four class kits: sword, shields, bow, arrow variants, dagger, staff, and thief tools (lockpick, coin, bottle, smoke bomb, noisemaker and tripwire traps, caltrops, water flask, sap).

Asset ids (21):
- `icon-item-sword-01`
- `icon-item-shield-wood-01`
- `icon-item-shield-metal-01`
- `icon-item-bow-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-standard-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-fire-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-water-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-rope-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-noise-01`
- `icon-item-arrow-blunt-01`
- `icon-item-dagger-01`
- `icon-item-staff-01`
- `icon-item-lockpick-iron-01`
- `icon-item-coin-01`
- `icon-item-bottle-01`
- `icon-item-smoke-bomb-01`
- `icon-item-trap-noisemaker-01`
- `icon-item-trap-tripwire-01`
- `icon-item-caltrops-01`
- `icon-item-water-flask-01`
- `icon-item-sap-01`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Consuming bead references and anchor/reference inputs (our own approved assets only)
- In: Output spec per template
- Out: Running the generator (see `e37-asset-icons-items-kit-generate`)
- Out: Changing a preamble (bible bead + version bump only)

Weapon icons use the approved weapon concepts as reference inputs. Loot/world item icons (potions, keys, treasures) are owned by the world/items asset set.

Prompts cite the locked style anchors from `e37-asset-style-lock` as reference inputs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 21 asset ids listed in this bead, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/`, then every id has exactly one prompt file whose asset id equals its filename stem and passes naming checks (`<category>-<subject>-<variant>`, ≤ 64 chars).
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble block with docs/art/style-bible.md §14, then it matches byte-for-byte and the correct §14.1 category add-on follows it.
- AC-3 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it names its consuming bead(s), output spec (1024² generate → 256²/128²/64² transparent, object ~80 % fill, ink drop shadow down-right) and the filled consistency checklist, with no unfilled `<…>` placeholders.
- AC-4 [content] Given the set, when reviewed against the bible, then every prompt writes out the palette hexes, shape language and silhouette rules needed to meet the approval criterion: every icon is identifiable at 64 px and arrow variants are distinguishable by head/payload shape, not colour alone.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that asks for text/letters, names an artist, studio or game, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails and names the file and line.

items.title: Generate kit item icons via Codex CLI
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every image candidate so the owner only has to approve (contract §6).

## What
Run `e37-image-gen-runner` (`codex exec` → gpt-image; fallback OpenAI Images API) for all 21 prompt files of `e37-asset-icons-items-kit-prompts`. Outputs land in `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` with a `vN.json` sidecar; Claude self-checks each candidate against its checklist, iterates, logs every iteration, then builds a batch review page for the owner.

## Scope
- In: Batch generation in planned batches respecting subscription limits
- In: Self-check + iteration log per asset
- In: Batch review page (contact sheet) for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e37-asset-icons-items-kit-approve`)
- Out: Committing final assets (integrate bead)

## Notes
Output spec: 1024² generate → 256²/128²/64² transparent, object ~80 % fill, ink drop shadow down-right. Record account tier in every sidecar — restrictive-tier outputs are placeholders only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 21 prompt files, when the runner batch completes, then `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.png` and a `vN.json` sidecar (prompt path, tool, model, account tier, date) exist for every id.
- AC-2 [content] Given each candidate, when checked against its output spec (1024² generate → 256²/128²/64² transparent, object ~80 % fill, ink drop shadow down-right), then dimensions, transparency/background and grid layout match or the iteration log records why it was regenerated.
- AC-3 [content] Given the batch review page, when opened, then it shows every id with its latest version, the prompt path and the checklist result.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given the image runner hits a usage/rate limit or network error mid-batch, when the batch is re-run, then it resumes from the first id without a candidate, never regenerates an id that already has a candidate or an approval record, and logs the back-off without printing any API key.
- AC-5 [integration] Given all sidecars and iteration logs, when the secret scanner runs, then no API key or token is found.

items.title: Owner approval: kit item icons
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the image gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the batch review page of 21 candidates and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: image, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e37-asset-icons-items-kit-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: every icon is identifiable at 64 px and arrow variants are distinguishable by head/payload shape, not colour alone. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 21 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "image".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then every icon is identifiable at 64 px and arrow variants are distinguishable by head/payload shape, not colour alone.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e37-asset-icons-items-kit-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

Final art replaces placeholders without touching gameplay code (contract §5: integration is a file swap).

- Out: Gameplay/UI logic (owned by the consuming beads)

items.acceptance:

items.title: Write core footsteps prompts (20 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Footsteps are both feedback and a stealth rule: players learn that gravel is loud because it sounds loud (loudness must match the sim noise radius).

## What
Write one prompt file per asset (or round-robin set) in `assets/prompts/sfx/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/sfx.md`, with the SFX PREAMBLE (audio bible §8) verbatim, the category add-on, sourcing (generated vs CC0), round-robin count, sim link, output spec and checklist.

Round-robin footstep sets (4–6 variants each) for stone, wood, dirt, grass, gravel and shallow water in sneak/walk/run gaits, plus light and heavy landings.

Asset ids (20):
- `sfx-foot-stone-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-stone-walk`
- `sfx-foot-stone-run`
- `sfx-foot-wood-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-wood-walk`
- `sfx-foot-wood-run`
- `sfx-foot-dirt-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-dirt-walk`
- `sfx-foot-dirt-run`
- `sfx-foot-grass-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-grass-walk`
- `sfx-foot-grass-run`
- `sfx-foot-gravel-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-gravel-walk`
- `sfx-foot-gravel-run`
- `sfx-foot-water-shallow-sneak`
- `sfx-foot-water-shallow-walk`
- `sfx-foot-water-shallow-run`
- `sfx-foot-land-light`
- `sfx-foot-land-heavy`

## Scope
- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Sim link (surface id / noise radius / element / creature state) per sound
- Out: Generation (`e38-asset-sfx-footsteps-core-generate`)

## Notes
Each id is a round-robin set (`-01`…`-04` minimum, per sfx template). Surface ids must equal `e09-sound-propagation` surface ids. m2 because the thief class gauntlet reads footstep loudness. CC0 sourcing (Kenney/freesound CC0) is acceptable and often better for footsteps. Sonic-lock anchor set.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 20 asset ids, when the asset validator runs over `assets/prompts/sfx/`, then each has exactly one prompt file whose id equals its filename stem and matches audio bible §6 naming.
- AC-2 [content] Given each prompt file, when the validator compares its preamble with docs/audio/audio-bible.md §8, then it matches byte-for-byte.
- AC-3 [content] Given each repeated sound, when inspected, then its round-robin count is ≥ 3 (footsteps 4–6) and its sim link names the sim id it must match.
- AC-4 [content] Given each prompt file, when inspected, then it states duration, mono/stereo, loop yes/no and loudness target from audio bible §5.1.
- AC-5 [content] Edge: given a prompt that requests intelligible speech, music, or contains an API key pattern, when the validator runs, then it fails naming the file.

items.title: Generate core footsteps via ElevenLabs or CC0
items.description:
## Why
Claude produces every SFX candidate end-to-end so the owner only listens (audio bible §9.1).

## What
Generate each prompt via `e38-sfx-gen-client` (or source CC0 per `e38-sfx-tool-decision`) into `assets/_incoming/<asset-id>/vN.wav`, run the audio import pipeline + validator, and build a listening page (playlist grouped by set, loudness readout).

## Scope
- In: Generation/sourcing, trimming, normalisation via pipeline
- In: Listening page for the approval bead
- Out: Owner approval (`e38-asset-sfx-footsteps-core-approve`)

## Notes
Record API tier / CC0 source URL per candidate. Paid tier for shipping sounds.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the 20 prompt files, when the batch completes, then every id (and every round-robin variant) has a `vN.wav` + sidecar (tool or source URL, licence, tier, date) in `assets/_incoming/`.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the candidates, when `e38-audio-validator` runs, then leading silence ≤ 10 ms, positional sounds are mono, loops have clean seams, and LUFS/true peak are within audio bible §5.1 tolerances.
- AC-3 [content] Given the listening page, when opened, then every id plays with its prompt path and loudness readout.

items.title: Owner approval: core footsteps
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the sfx batch gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the listening page of 20 sounds and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: sfx batch, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e38-asset-sfx-footsteps-core-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: loudness ordering sneak < walk < run < land holds, and surfaces order carpet < grass < dirt < stone < wood-hollow < gravel/water when auditioned in sequence. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the review page, when the owner finishes the session, then each of the 20 ids has an approve or reject decision with notes recorded in `assets/approvals.json` for gate "sfx batch".
- AC-2 [manual] Given the approved items viewed side by side, when the owner compares them, then loudness ordering sneak < walk < run < land holds, and surfaces order carpet < grass < dirt < stone < wood-hollow < gravel/water when auditioned in sequence.
- AC-3 [integration] Edge: given a rejected id, when its decision is recorded, then it is re-queued for `e38-asset-sfx-footsteps-core-generate` with the owner note in its iteration log, and no already-approved id is regenerated.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an approval record whose SHA-256 does not match the file promoted to `assets/source/`, when CI runs, then the approval check fails naming the id.

items.title: Owner approval: stealth action SFX
items.description:
## Why
Every shipped asset needs an owner decision at the sfx batch gate; CI refuses final assets without one (contract §6).

## What
The owner reviews the listening page of 20 sounds and approves or rejects each item with a note. Claude records every decision in `assets/approvals.json` (asset id, gate: sfx batch, version, SHA-256, approver, date, notes). Rejected items loop back to `e38-asset-sfx-stealth-actions-generate` with the note appended to their iteration log.

## Scope
- In: Owner decision per asset
- In: Approval records written by Claude
- In: Re-queue of rejected items
- Out: Generation or editing by the owner — the owner never edits assets

## Notes
Approval criteria: no sound contains intelligible words, and loud world events (bell, shatter) are clearly louder than thief actions. Batch reviews are designed to take ≤ 15 minutes of owner time.

items.title: Write UI SFX prompts (14 assets)
items.description:
## Why
Menus should feel like handling a field journal — paper, leather, brass (audio bible §7.6) — and critical HUD states (lock-on, low health) need audio.

## What
Write one prompt file per asset (or round-robin set) in `assets/prompts/sfx/<asset-id>.md` from `_templates/sfx.md`, with the SFX PREAMBLE (audio bible §8) verbatim, the category add-on, sourcing (generated vs CC0), round-robin count, sim link, output spec and checklist.

Menu open/close (leather flap), hover, confirm (brass click), cancel, page turn, coin clink, item pickup, equip, quest update (soft chime), journal quill scratch, error/deny (wooden knock), lock-on tick and low-health heartbeat loop.

Asset ids (14):
- `sfx-ui-menu-open-01`
- `sfx-ui-menu-close-01`
- `sfx-ui-hover-01`
- `sfx-ui-confirm-01`
- `sfx-ui-cancel-01`
- `sfx-ui-page-turn-01`
- `sfx-ui-coin-01`
- `sfx-ui-item-pickup-01`
- `sfx-ui-equip-01`
- `sfx-ui-quest-update-01`
- `sfx-ui-journal-quill-01`
- `sfx-ui-error-deny-01`
- `sfx-ui-lockon-01`
- `sfx-ui-low-health-heartbeat-loop-01`

- In: One prompt file per asset id above
- In: Sim link (surface id / noise radius / element / creature state) per sound
- Out: Generation (`e38-asset-sfx-ui-core-generate`)

- In: Post-processing, encode, CREDITS, approval records, data binding
- Out: Adaptive music controller logic (`e28-adaptive-music`)

## Notes
Consumers: `e28-adaptive-music`, `e09-alert-barks`, `e19-capabilities-screen`, `e38-music-state-data`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the approved takes, when processed, then each stinger is −16 LUFS ±1 (short-term max), ≤ −1.0 dBTP, transient within 20 ms of start and tail ≤ 2 s, and `e38-audio-validator` is green.
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/CREDITS.md`, when audited, then each stinger has a row with Suno tier, date and prompt path, plus an approval record.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the stealth course and capabilities screen, when a guard cycles suspicious→detected→lost and a verb is learned, then the final stingers play on the music bus without clipping.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given a stinger without an approval record, when the build runs, then its placeholder remains and the report lists it.

items.title: Lock approved style anchor images for all later image prompts
items.description:
## Why
Generative tools drift; locking a few approved images as series anchors keeps 300+ later assets looking like one game (style bible §12).

## What
After the first anchor sets (player class sheets, school frames + spell icons, core menu kit) are approved, Claude proposes 1–3 anchor images per category (character, prop, icon, UI, VFX, key art) with rationale; the owner confirms. Anchors are recorded in `assets/prompts/_anchors.json` (category → asset ids + SHA-256) and every later prompt file must list its category anchors as reference inputs.

## Scope
- In: Anchor proposal + owner confirmation
- In: Anchor registry file
- In: Validator rule: non-anchor prompt files must cite their category anchors
- Out: Changing the style bible itself (bible bead + version bump)

## Notes
Anchor sets: `e37-asset-player-classes-*`, `e37-asset-school-identity-*`, `e37-asset-spell-icons-*`, `e37-asset-ui-menus-journal-*`. VFX anchors may be added after the first VFX set is approved (registry is append-only with owner sign-off).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the approved anchor sets, when the owner reviews the proposal, then anchors for character, prop, icon and UI categories are confirmed and recorded in `assets/approvals.json` with gate "style-lock".
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/prompts/_anchors.json`, when validated, then every anchor id resolves to an approved asset whose SHA-256 matches its approval record.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a non-anchor image prompt file that omits its category anchors, when the asset validator runs, then it fails naming the file.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given an anchor asset that is later replaced (hash change), when CI runs, then the validator flags every prompt file citing the old hash for re-review instead of passing silently.

items.title: Lock approved reference sounds for all later SFX prompts
items.description:
## Why
SFX generated in many batches drift in loudness, room tone and weight; locked reference sounds keep the palette coherent (audio bible §7).

## What
After the knight combat, impact/Forgotten and core footstep sets are approved, Claude proposes reference sounds per SFX category (impact, weapon, footstep, creature, magic-to-follow, UI) with measured loudness; the owner confirms. Recorded in `assets/prompts/_sonic-anchors.json`; later SFX prompt files cite them and the generate step loudness-matches against them.

## Scope
- In: Reference proposal + owner confirmation
- In: Sonic anchor registry
- In: Validator rule for later SFX prompt files
- Out: Music (Suno) — stingers follow the audio bible directly

## Notes
Anchor sets: `e38-asset-sfx-knight-combat-*`, `e38-asset-sfx-impacts-forgotten-*`, `e38-asset-sfx-footsteps-core-*`.

- AC-1 [manual] Given the approved anchor sets, when the owner reviews the proposal, then references for impact, weapon, footstep and creature categories are confirmed and recorded in `assets/approvals.json` with gate "sonic-lock".
- AC-2 [content] Given `assets/prompts/_sonic-anchors.json`, when validated, then every reference id resolves to an approved sound whose SHA-256 matches its approval record.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a later SFX prompt file without its category references, when the asset validator runs, then it fails naming the file.
- AC-4 [integration] Edge: given a new candidate whose integrated loudness deviates > 3 LU from its category reference, when the generate step runs, then it is flagged on the listening page rather than silently accepted.
